# cleura_gardener_authentication_configuration (Resource)

Defines the **OIDC issuers** that Gardener clusters accept sign-ins from: an identity provider such as Keycloak, Entra ID or Dex, the audiences (client IDs) it issues tokens for, and how token claims map to Kubernetes user names and groups.
One configuration can be attached to any number of clusters in the region with [`cleura_gardener_shoot.authentication_configuration_name`](gardener_shoot.md); the same configuration is visible to every project in the account.

Users then sign in with a kubeconfig from [`cleura_gardener_shoot_oidc_kubeconfig`](../data-sources/gardener_shoot_oidc_kubeconfig.md), which needs the [kubelogin](https://github.com/int128/kubelogin) plugin (`kubectl oidc-login`).
The cluster sees them as `oidc:<alias>:<username>` with groups `oidc:<alias>:<group>`, where `<alias>` is the key in `issuers`; role bindings refer to those names.
A new cluster has no role bindings, so the first binding is created with an admin kubeconfig.
Group names come through exactly as the identity provider sends them: a Keycloak group mapper with "Full group path" on sends `/k8s-admin`, so the binding subject is `oidc:keycloak:/k8s-admin`.

- `issuers` is keyed by an alias of your choice (3–32 characters, lowercase letters, digits and `-`).
  Each issuer's `url` must be `https` and unique within the configuration; several audiences for one issuer go in its `audiences` list.
- `certificate_authority` takes the issuer's CA as PEM; the provider encodes it.
  It is not needed for certificates from a public CA.
- Changes to an attached configuration are applied in place.
  Removing `authentication_configuration_name` from a cluster, or destroying the configuration after its clusters have moved elsewhere, detaches it.
- The configuration can't be deleted while a cluster uses it.
  To move clusters to a new configuration and delete the old one in the same apply, set `lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }`, so Terraform updates the clusters before deleting the configuration.

### Prerequisites

The provider must be authenticated and have a `cloud` and `region`; `project_id` is not needed.
See the provider's [Authentication](../index.md#authentication) documentation.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Accept OIDC tokens from a Keycloak realm on Gardener clusters. Users sign in
# as "oidc:keycloak:<username>" and carry their groups as
# "oidc:keycloak:<group>", which is what role bindings refer to.
resource "cleura_gardener_authentication_configuration" "sso" {
  name = "corp-sso"

  issuers = {
    keycloak = {
      url       = "https://keycloak.example.com/realms/platform"
      audiences = ["kube-api"] # the OIDC client ID(s) kubectl signs in with

      # Only needed when the issuer's certificate is not from a public CA.
      # certificate_authority = file("${path.module}/keycloak-ca.pem")

      claim_mappings = {
        username = { claim = "preferred_username" }
        groups   = { claim = "groups" }
      }

      user_validation_rules = [
        { expression = "!user.username.startsWith(\"system:\")", message = "username cannot use the reserved system: prefix" },
      ]
    }
  }

  # When clusters are moved to another configuration and this one is removed
  # in the same apply, update the clusters before deleting it.
  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }
}

# Attach it to a cluster. Changing or removing it updates the cluster in place.
resource "cleura_gardener_shoot" "example" {
  name               = "example-cluster"
  kubernetes_version = "1.35.9"

  authentication_configuration_name = cleura_gardener_authentication_configuration.sso.name

  shoot_provider = {
    infrastructure_config = {
      floating_pool_name = "ext-net"
    }
    load_balancer_provider = "amphora"
    workers = [{
      name = "wg1"
      machine = {
        image_name    = "gardenlinux"
        image_version = "1877.24.0"
        type          = "b.2c4gb"
      }
      volume_size = "50Gi"
    }]
  }
}
```

## Import

```shell
# An authentication configuration is imported by its name.
terraform import cleura_gardener_authentication_configuration.sso corp-sso
```

## Schema

### Required

- `issuers` (Attributes Map) The identity providers, keyed by alias: 3 to 32 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. The alias is part of the user and group names a cluster sees (`oidc:<alias>:`) and selects the issuer when fetching a kubeconfig. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--issuers))
- `name` (String) Name of the configuration: up to 32 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit. Changing it creates a new configuration.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Identifier of the configuration: its `name`. Also the import ID.

<a id="nestedatt--issuers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `issuers`

Required:

- `audiences` (List of String) Accepted audiences, usually the OIDC client IDs. A token is accepted if its `aud` claim contains at least one of them.
- `claim_mappings` (Attributes) How token claims become the Kubernetes user. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--issuers--claim_mappings))
- `url` (String) Issuer URL. Must use `https`, contain no username, password, query or fragment, match the `iss` claim of the tokens exactly, and be unique within the configuration.

Optional:

- `audience_match_policy` (String) How `audiences` is matched against a token's `aud` claim. Only `MatchAny` (the default) is supported: the claim must contain at least one of the audiences.
- `certificate_authority` (String) PEM-encoded CA certificate(s) used to verify the issuer's TLS certificate, for example `file("ca.pem")`. Leave it out when the issuer uses a publicly trusted certificate.
- `claim_validation_rules` (Attributes) Rules a token's claims must satisfy. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--issuers--claim_validation_rules))
- `user_validation_rules` (Attributes List) CEL expressions over the resulting user that must evaluate to true. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--issuers--user_validation_rules))

<a id="nestedatt--issuers--claim_mappings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `issuers.claim_mappings`

Required:

- `username` (Attributes) The claim that becomes the user name. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--issuers--claim_mappings--username))

Optional:

- `extra` (Attributes List) Extra attributes added to the user. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--issuers--claim_mappings--extra))
- `groups` (Attributes) Where the user's groups come from: exactly one of `claim` or `expression`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--issuers--claim_mappings--groups))
- `uid` (Attributes) The claim that becomes the user's UID. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--issuers--claim_mappings--uid))

<a id="nestedatt--issuers--claim_mappings--username"></a>
### Nested Schema for `issuers.claim_mappings.username`

Required:

- `claim` (String) Claim to use, e.g. `email` or `preferred_username`.

Read-Only:

- `prefix` (String) Prefix added to the user name, set by Cleura (`oidc:<alias>:`).


<a id="nestedatt--issuers--claim_mappings--extra"></a>
### Nested Schema for `issuers.claim_mappings.extra`

Required:

- `key` (String) Attribute key, a lowercase domain-prefixed path such as `example.com/team`.
- `value_expression` (String) CEL expression that yields the value.


<a id="nestedatt--issuers--claim_mappings--groups"></a>
### Nested Schema for `issuers.claim_mappings.groups`

Optional:

- `claim` (String) Claim that holds the groups, e.g. `groups`.
- `expression` (String) CEL expression that yields the groups.

Read-Only:

- `prefix` (String) Prefix added to group names, set by Cleura: `oidc:<alias>:` when groups come from a `claim`, none when they come from an `expression`.


<a id="nestedatt--issuers--claim_mappings--uid"></a>
### Nested Schema for `issuers.claim_mappings.uid`

Required:

- `claim` (String) Claim to use, e.g. `sub`.

Read-Only:

- `prefix` (String) Prefix added to the UID, set by Cleura.



<a id="nestedatt--issuers--claim_validation_rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `issuers.claim_validation_rules`

Optional:

- `claim_rules` (Attributes List) Claims that must have a given value. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--issuers--claim_validation_rules--claim_rules))
- `expression_rules` (Attributes List) CEL expressions over the claims that must evaluate to true. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--issuers--claim_validation_rules--expression_rules))

<a id="nestedatt--issuers--claim_validation_rules--claim_rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `issuers.claim_validation_rules.claim_rules`

Required:

- `claim` (String) Claim name.
- `required_value` (String) Value the claim must have.


<a id="nestedatt--issuers--claim_validation_rules--expression_rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `issuers.claim_validation_rules.expression_rules`

Required:

- `expression` (String) CEL expression that must evaluate to true.
- `message` (String) Message returned when the expression is false.



<a id="nestedatt--issuers--user_validation_rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `issuers.user_validation_rules`

Required:

- `expression` (String) CEL expression that must evaluate to true.
- `message` (String) Message returned when the expression is false.
